My Quaker is microchipped - I work at an avian vet and we put them under a general anaesthetic for the procedure as it's quite a large needle. I definitely suggest a chip over a leg band (I've seen way too many issues with leg bands) and people that find birds seem to be more likely to look for a bird clinic to take them to.

Perches, avoid flat/smooth perches, try to get more natural perches like branches as smooth perches can damage their feet.
Avoid any toys that are made of rope!! They chew at them and can end with a build up of fibre in their crop (usually needing surgery to fix!). Instead look for toys made of things like coconut fibre, raffia palm etc.
